about: Ground truth of the Lecture 1 toy data: a simulated PennCATH-like case-control study of coronary artery disease (toy.*) and a 1000-Genomes-like reference panel (toy_1kg.*). See data/README.md.

conventions.snp_ids: tsnp + 5 digits, numbered in genome order over all study and reference SNPs; not dbSNP rsIDs
conventions.study_sample_ids: FID = a unique number from 80001 written in literal double quotes, IID = 1 (the PennCATH convention); PAT = MAT = 0 for everyone, relatives included
conventions.reference_sample_ids: TG + 5 digits; FID = IID = the panel's sample value; they are not 1000 Genomes IDs
conventions.positions: GRCh37-like base-pair positions on chromosomes 1-22; the cM column is 0
conventions.alleles: ref/alt are forward-strand (GRCh37 + strand) alleles, as in toy_1kg.bim; toy.bim reports the SNPs listed in features.f_reference_merge.study_reverse_strand_count on the reverse strand (complemented alleles)
conventions.genotypes_in_files: A1 is the minor allele of each file (as PLINK writes it); the .bed counts A1 alleles
conventions.keys: people are keyed by the exact FID and IID strings of toy.fam (quotes included); SNPs by their toy.bim ID

a_variant_missingness.intended: --geno 0.01 on toy removes every planted SNP (call rate below 99%) plus a few ordinary SNPs whose sporadic missing calls happen to exceed 1% (2.5 of 250 people, so 3 or more missing calls)

b_sample_missingness.intended: after --geno 0.01, --mind 0.01 removes exactly the degraded samples; --mind 0.01 on the raw data would also remove the low-quality samples (and any ordinary person just above 1%), whose missing calls sit mostly in the SNPs that --geno removes. This is why the practical filters SNPs first.

c_hardy_weinberg.intended: the six artifact SNPs have UNAFF exact-test p < 1e-8 (also in the ALL and AFF rows); the causal SNP departs from HWE in the AFF rows (heterozygote deficit among cases) but not in the UNAFF rows; no other SNP reaches UNAFF p < 1e-8. The SNPs in stratification_examples (not planted) reach p < 1e-8 in the ALL rows only: their allele frequencies differ strongly between the European-like majority and the other ancestries, and pooling populations gives a heterozygote deficit (Wahlund effect). Exact p-values from the lab emulator: lab_view.hardy

causal_snp.model: penetrance (risk of CAD) by number of risk alleles: 0.01, 0.01, 0.2 (nearly recessive, genotype relative risk 20 for two copies); cases are drawn in proportion to penetrance and controls in proportion to 1 - penetrance; deliberately exaggerated so that 81 cases show the effect (real CAD variants have odds ratios of about 1.1-1.3 per allele)

d_relatedness.note: realized = shares of study SNPs where the two people carry 0, 1 or 2 haplotypes inherited from the same founder haplotype (simulated meiosis with Poisson crossovers)
d_relatedness.unrelated_pairs: counts of unplanted pairs above PI_HAT 0.1875 and 0.1, by the groups of the two people, are in lab_view.genome.unrelated_pairs_above
d_relatedness.intended: --genome on the LD-pruned QC'd data shows the duplicate (PI_HAT near 1), the parent-offspring pair (Z1 near 1), the full siblings (Z0, Z1, Z2 near 0.25, 0.5, 0.25) and the half siblings (Z0, Z1 near 0.5, PI_HAT near 0.25, above every unplanted pair that does not involve the contaminated sample). The contaminated sample has PI_HAT of about 0.17 with everyone (up to about 0.27), so it makes up the unplanted pairs above 0.1875: a DNA mixture has extra heterozygous calls and therefore almost never shows opposite homozygotes (IBS0) with anyone, which the method-of-moments estimator reads as shared ancestry. One person related to everybody points to contamination, which --het confirms. Other unplanted pairs reach PI_HAT of about 0.15-0.19 through estimation noise with about 2,500 pruned SNPs (most pairs above 0.1 are such noise), which is why no pair more distant than half siblings was planted

e_heterozygosity.contamination_model: DNA mixture: B-allele signal b = (1 - alpha) g1/2 + alpha g2/2 + noise (alpha 0.29, noise SD 0.04); called heterozygous when 0.2 < b < 0.8; a call at a site where the two genotypes differ is missing with probability 0.006
e_heterozygosity.ancestry_effect: F in --het compares each person's homozygosity with what the allele frequencies of the whole, mostly European-like sample predict. Admixed people have negative F: their two haplotypes come partly from different populations, so they are heterozygous more often than European frequencies predict. East-Asian-like people have positive F: drift since the out-of-Africa split left them less heterozygous at these SNPs. African-like and South-Asian-like people have F near 0 (African-like people are more diverse overall, but the SNPs were chosen to be common in Europeans). Values by group: lab_view.het.F_by_group
e_heterozygosity.intended: both rules flag the contaminated sample (F far below -0.1; heterozygosity rate far above the mean + 3 SD; its raw missingness is also raised, but stays below 1%) and the inbred person (F near 0.25; rate far below the mean - 3 SD). The two rules nearly coincide: 3 SD of the heterozygosity rate is about 0.04-0.045, which is about 0.12 in F units, so they differ only for people with |F| between 0.1 and about 0.12, such as admixed people with large African-like shares and ordinary people who pass |F| = 0.1 by chance with about 2,500 pruned SNPs. The contamination also lowers the sample's IBS0 with everyone, which raises its PI_HAT in --genome (see d_relatedness). Exact lists from the lab emulator: lab_view.het

f_reference_merge.study_reverse_strand_snps_note: for these SNPs toy.bim lists the complement of the forward-strand alleles; only the shared ones matter for --bmerge
f_reference_merge.intended: --bmerge of the QC'd study with toy_1kg fails with 'variants with 3+ alleles present' and writes <out>-merge.missnp listing expected_missnp; after --flip with that list the merge succeeds; the strand-swapped A/T and C/G SNPs merge silently with their alleles exchanged (their study allele frequencies mirror the reference's); after the merge, --geno 0.1 drops every SNP that is in only one fileset

g_ancestry.intended: GrafAnc (lab emulator) assigns the European-like people to EUR, African-like to AFR, East-Asian-like to EAS and South-Asian-like to SAS; South-Asian-like people lie between the EUR and EAS vertices (their ASI ancestry); admixed people lie between EUR and AFR in GD1/GD2, at positions that follow their African-like share, so their group depends on that share. In the merged PCA with toy_1kg, the admixed people lie between the EUR and AFR clusters and the South-Asian-like people between EUR and EAS in the same way

long_range_ld_region.model: two haplotype clades (standard and inverted orientation, as at the 8p23.1 inversion) with no recombination between clades; 72 SNPs tag the clade, the rest vary within one clade
long_range_ld_region.intended: in an unpruned study PCA (--maf 0.05 --pca without --extract) one of the top PCs sorts people by the number of inverted copies (0, 1, 2); after LD pruning only a few region SNPs remain, and the region no longer drives any of the top PCs (at most a weak echo on a late PC)

lab_view.about: Steps 1-5 of the practical run on toy.* inside the generator by the lab's PLINK emulator (assets/js/lab/plink-core.js): --geno 0.01, then --mind 0.01, --hardy, --indep-pairwise 50 5 0.3, and --genome and --het with --extract of the pruned SNPs. These are the numbers the in-browser lab shows; real PLINK 1.9.0 gives the same (tools/real_plink_check.mjs). Regenerate the data if plink-core.js changes.
